common_name: Merry Christmas Rex Begonia (Red-and-Silver Zoned Rhizomatous Begonia)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant or move containers to a sheltered, deep-shade spot outdoors after all frost danger has passed.

directions: Grow in bright, indirect light with no direct midday sun, which quickly scorches the vivid foliage. Each spiraled leaf carries a deep red central zone bordered by a silvery-white band and a dark green outer margin, a color pattern that holds strongest with steady humidity above 50 percent and consistent 14-16 hour day length under grow lights in winter. Keep the rhizome barely moist and let the surface dry slightly between waterings to prevent rot, and increase humidity with a pebble tray rather than misting the leaves directly. Propagate by wedge or whole-leaf cuttings laid on moist media, which root readily at the cut veins within a few weeks.
sources: American Begonia Society — Rex Cultorum Variety Notes

common_name: Irene Nuss Begonia (Pink-Flowered Bronze-Leaf Superba Cane Begonia)

planting.note: Move potted canes outdoors to a bright, sheltered, partly shaded spot once nights stay above 50°F; stake tall canes as they grow.

directions: Plant in bright, filtered light in a rich, fast-draining potting mix, since this vigorous superba-type hybrid of 'Lenore Olivier' and 'Kentwood' quickly builds tall, jointed canes topped with deeply scalloped bronze-green leaves and wine-red undersides. Pinch young canes to encourage branching and a fuller silhouette, and stake older canes if they lean under the weight of foliage. Drooping clusters of bright pink flowers appear from late spring into summer, held well above the leaves. Let the topsoil dry slightly between waterings and feed lightly through the growing season to sustain the oversized leaf display.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit Records

common_name: Orange Rubra Begonia (Silver-Spotted Cane Begonia with Orange Flowers)

planting.note: Set containers outdoors in a bright, sheltered, partly shaded position after the last frost; bring indoors well before the first fall frost.

directions: Grow in bright, filtered light protected from hot afternoon sun, which can bleach the silver-spotted, lance-shaped leaves. The upright, jointed cane stems carry pendulous clusters of bright orange flowers that appear intermittently through most of the year rather than in one flush. Pinch young stems early to build a bushier plant, since unpinched canes grow tall and leggy. Water when the top inch of soil dries, and repot in spring only when the rhizomatous roots crowd the container.

common_name: Beefsteak Begonia (Round-Leaf Rhizomatous Begonia with Red-Backed Foliage)

planting.note: Grow year-round indoors or move pots to a sheltered, shaded outdoor spot once nights stay reliably above 50°F.

directions: One of the oldest begonia hybrids still in wide cultivation, raised in Germany in 1845 from Begonia manicata and Begonia hydrocotylifolia, this rhizomatous begonia forms glossy, rounded, olive-green leaves with a deep red underside and a thin fringe of red hairs along the edge. Grow in bright, indirect light, since it tolerates lower light levels than many rhizomatous types but colors best with a few hours of gentle morning sun. Let the surface of the mix dry between waterings to protect the thick, creeping rhizome from rot, and keep humidity moderate to high for steady growth. Propagate by rhizome division or leaf-petiole cuttings, both of which root readily in a humid environment.
sources: American Begonia Society — Rhizomatous Begonia Variety Classification
